name: Hindsight
tagline: A long-term memory service for AI agents - they store what they learn, recall it later, and get better over time.
sentence: Give your AI agent a persistent memory so it remembers your preferences, past decisions and project context across sessions - like a digital notebook it reads before every conversation.

visual.alt: Diagram showing Hindsight's three operations: Retain (green arrow storing information into World Facts, Experiences, Opinions and Observations), Recall (blue arrow retrieving information), and Reflect (purple arrow generating new insights from stored memories).
visual.caption: Three operations: Retain stores facts, Recall retrieves them, Reflect synthesizes new insights across memories.

board.say: Your AI agent forgets everything between sessions - it asks the same questions, misses context, and starts from scratch every time.
board.eg: You tell your coding agent your project uses PostgreSQL and prefers tabs over spaces. Next session, it suggests MySQL and uses spaces.

board.say: Your agent calls Hindsight's 'retain' operation after each conversation, and 'recall' before the next one.
board.eg: At the end of a coding session, the agent sends its notes to Hindsight. Before the next session, it asks Hindsight what it knows about this project.

board.say: Conversations, facts, decisions and preferences - anything the agent should remember later.
board.eg: A conversation where you told the agent 'always use TypeScript, never JavaScript' and 'deploy to the staging server first'.

board.say: It breaks conversations into facts, stores them, and builds a picture of what it knows over time.
steps: Retain: breaks the input into individual facts and relationships, stores them with timestamps and context
Recall: searches stored memories using four strategies at once (meaning, keywords, connections and time) and ranks the best matches
Reflect: looks across many memories to answer questions that need reasoning, like 'what patterns does this user follow?'
board.eg: After 20 sessions, Hindsight has built a profile: this user prefers TypeScript, deploys to staging first, and reviews PRs on Monday mornings.

board.say: An agent that remembers what you told it, learns your preferences, and gets more useful over time.

outputs.eg: The agent recalls that you use PostgreSQL without being told again
After several sessions, Hindsight consolidates 'prefers tabs' into a standing observation the agent always sees
A 'mental model' page answers 'what are this user's coding preferences?' without searching each time

before: Your AI agent forgets everything between sessions. You repeat your preferences, your project context, and your past decisions every time.
There is no shared memory across agents - if you use Claude Code and another tool, each one starts from zero.
You keep a manual notes file of context to paste into each new session.
after: The agent remembers your preferences, past decisions and project context across sessions, and they improve over time as it consolidates what it learns.
Multiple agents share the same memory, so switching between tools does not mean starting over.
Standing 'mental model' pages answer common questions instantly, without searching or calling an AI model each time.

steps: [Read the quickstart guide](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/getting-started/quickstart) to choose your install method: a container image, a Python package, or the managed cloud service.

Run the container image with your AI provider key: `docker run -d -p 8888:8888 -p 9999:9999 -e OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key ghcr.io/vectorize-io/hindsight:latest`. Open [localhost:9999](http://localhost:9999) to see the dashboard.
Install the Python or Node.js client and try the retain-recall-reflect cycle from [the cookbook](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/guides).

footprint.disk: Container image: no data found for image size. Python package (hindsight-all): large dependency tree including PyTorch - one reviewer ran out of space in a 2 GB container. Binary downloads: about 3-4 MB per platform (macOS ARM 2.8 MB, Linux x64 4.1 MB). Needs a PostgreSQL database with pgvector.
footprint.memory: No data found. Requires a running PostgreSQL instance and an AI provider key for the extract step.
footprint.runs_on: Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel - Intel is limited, use the slim package), Windows (x86_64). Also available as a managed cloud service.

best_for: You build AI agents that talk to the same users repeatedly and need to remember past conversations and preferences
You want agents that improve over time by consolidating what they learn into reusable knowledge
skip_if: You only use AI agents for one-off tasks - persistent memory adds complexity with no payoff if there is nothing to remember
You need a simple key-value store - Hindsight's retain-recall-reflect pipeline requires an AI provider key and a database, which is heavy for basic storage
You want something that works without any cloud AI service - Hindsight needs an AI provider for fact extraction

alternatives.name: Mem0
alternatives.line: Another open-source agent memory system. Graph features are behind a paid Pro tier at $249 per month.

alternatives.name: Zep
alternatives.line: Open-core agent memory with a managed cloud option. Scored 71.2% on the LongMemEval benchmark versus Hindsight's claimed 94.6%.

watch: **Benchmark numbers are self-reported.** The project claims 94.6% on LongMemEval and says Virginia Tech and The Washington Post independently reproduced the results, but the reproduction details are on the vendor's own site.

**The pip install is very large.** One reviewer's install failed after 226 seconds in a 2 GB container because the dependency tree (including PyTorch) ran out of space. Start with the container image instead.

**Commercial company behind it.** Vectorize.io offers a managed cloud service and an enterprise tier. The open-source project is MIT-licensed today, but the company's business model may shape future development.
**Fortune 500 claims are unverified.** The project says it is used in production at Fortune 500 enterprises, but names no companies and no independent source confirms this.
